project.title: Plant Disease Classifier Reliability Study
project.short_description: A pre-registered, leakage-audited study testing whether plant disease classifiers that score ~99% on PlantVillage stay reliable on field style PlantDoc photos, and whether their confidence can be trusted to say “I don’t know.” It compares a scratch CNN with a fine-tuned ResNet-18 across three seeds.
project.overview: Plant disease classifiers routinely report ~99% accuracy on PlantVillage, a dataset of single leaves photographed on plain backgrounds. Real field photos look nothing like that. This study trains two models on PlantVillage: a from scratch CNN and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18. It then tests them exactly once on PlantDoc, a dataset of web-sourced, field style images. The study measures three things: how far accuracy falls, whether the models’ confidence stays honest, and whether a confidence based “abstain when unsure” rule still works. The research questions, hypotheses, metrics and decision rules were all fixed and committed to git before any external data was touched. Every result, including the negative ones, is reported with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals.
project.problem_statement:
High in-distribution accuracy is often taken to mean a model is ready for real use. For plant disease detection, that assumption is risky: a confident wrong diagnosis can lead to the wrong treatment. The study asked five questions:

  1. How much does accuracy drop from PlantVillage to field style PlantDoc images?
  2. Does ImageNet pre-training (ResNet-18) generalize better than a scratch CNN?
  3. Are the models’ confidence scores calibrated on the external set, and does temperature scaling fix them?
  4. Can a confidence threshold set on source data make the model abstain safely on new data?
  5. Which classes and errors drive the failures? (exploratory)
project.dataset_info:
• Source (training/validation/test): PlantVillage colour images. The audit covered 54,305 images, and the study used 23 classes that map to PlantDoc. Images were grouped by leaf so the same leaf never appears in two splits. Same class near duplicates (DCT perceptual hash distance ≤ 2) were merged.
  • Split: leaf group aware 70 / 7.5 / 7.5 / 15 (train / validation-for-selection / validation-for-calibration / test), split seed 42. No group or hash overlaps across splits or with the external set.
  • External (evaluation only): PlantDoc “cropped” release, 2,578 images audited. After de-duplication, removing clusters with conflicting labels, and mapping to PlantVillage classes, the primary set is 23 classes, 1,993 images, with at least 53 per class. It was never used for training, tuning, calibration or thresholds.
  • Integrity: the dataset files are checked against SHA-256 manifests (35,410 files) on every fresh runtime. The audit found no exact image overlap between the two datasets.
  • Licensing: PlantDoc is CC BY 4.0. The PlantVillage licence couldn’t be confirmed from primary sources, so the datasets aren’t redistributed; only hashes and file lists are.
project.methodology:
• Pre-registration: the protocol (v1.0, tagged in git) fixed four hypotheses, the primary metrics and the decision rules. Later amendments are dated and logged.
  • Data audit and dataset freeze: duplicates, label conflicts, near duplicates and cross dataset overlap were checked. The class list, mapping, thresholds, manifests and transform were then hashed and committed before training.
  • Models: a scratch CNN (3.4M parameters) and an ImageNet pretrained ResNet-18 (11.2M parameters). Both used the same input size (224×224), loss (cross-entropy without label smoothing), optimizer (AdamW), augmentation, early stopping and seeds 1, 2 and 3.
  • Tuning on source data only: three learning rates per model, chosen by validation loss. The checkpoint was chosen by lowest validation NLL.
  • Calibration and abstention: one temperature per run, fitted on the calibration split. Two abstention thresholds came from that split: R-cov (keep 90% coverage) and R-risk (≤1% error).
  • Run freeze: temperature, thresholds, checkpoint SHA-256 and code commit were committed per run before any PlantDoc inference. The evaluator refuses to run if verification fails.
  • One external pass and statistics:
    • Metrics: accuracy, macro-F1, ECE (15 bins), Brier, NLL, selective risk and coverage, AURC, and AUROC for error detection.
    • Intervals: 10,000 resample cluster bootstrap, plus paired intervals for the model comparison.
    • Seeds are reported individually, never averaged into an ensemble.
project.implementation_details:
• Library (src/plantrel): data loading, models, trainer with fp16 and checkpoint/resume, calibration, metrics, bootstrap, hashing, freeze verifier, audit and report modules.
  • Pipeline scripts: dataset audit and splits, Colab data preparation (clones datasets at pinned revisions and verifies every file hash), training, calibration, run freeze creation, final external evaluation and result aggregation.
  • Freeze system: JSON freezes with SHA-256 files in configs/frozen/. The verifier uses two independent git protections, so frozen choices can’t change silently.
  • Training: Google Colab Tesla T4, Python 3.13, PyTorch 2.11, torchvision 0.26, about 17 minutes per run, 6 final runs (2 models × 3 seeds).
  • Testing: 229 pytest tests covering metrics, bootstrap, checkpointing/resume, the freeze verifier and the training loop.
  • Reporting: scripts generate the tables and figures from results/results.json. An interactive static results explorer is published on GitHub Pages.
  • Transparency: the first external run crashed on a JSON serialization bug before any metric was seen. The fix was committed and the run freezes were re-issued with byte identical temperatures, thresholds and checkpoint hashes (amendment A3.1).
project.results:
• Large collapse under distribution shift (H1 supported). Accuracy fell from 0.987–0.996 on the PlantVillage test set to 0.143–0.167 on PlantDoc, a gap of about 83 percentage points for both models. The 95% intervals sit at roughly 81–86 pp in every seed. Chance level with 23 classes is 4.3%.
  • ResNet-18 vs scratch CNN: not demonstrated (H2 not supported). ResNet-18 had a higher macro F1 in all three seeds (+0.004 to +0.019), but the paired interval excluded zero in only one seed. ImageNet pre-training didn’t buy measurable robustness here.
  • Severe overconfidence (H3 supported). External ECE was 0.65–0.74, against 0.003–0.005 in-distribution. Temperature scaling fitted on source data made it slightly worse: the fitted temperature was below 1 (0.48–0.85), so it sharpened the predictions.
  • Abstention barely helps, and thresholds don’t transfer (H4 supported). On PlantDoc, confidence separates right from wrong answers only slightly better than chance (AUROC 0.59–0.63, against 0.97–0.99 in-distribution).
    • The 90%-coverage rule accepted only 8–19% of PlantDoc images.
    • The ≤1%-risk rule accepted 89–99% of images at an 82–86% error rate.
  • Takeaway: in-distribution accuracy and calibration say almost nothing about field reliability, and fixes tuned on source data don’t solve a distribution shift problem.
project.future_improvements:
• Have a plant pathologist review the PlantVillage→PlantDoc class mapping.
  • Collect a small labelled field sample, kept separate from evaluation, to test target-domain calibration.
  • Try domain robust training methods, more architectures and more dataset pairs.
  • Build a small Streamlit inference demo and record a walkthrough video.
project.my_role:
I designed and carried out the study end to end. That covered:

  • writing the experimental protocol and the literature review
  • auditing both datasets for duplicates, label conflicts and cross dataset leakage
  • building leaf group aware splits and the hashed dataset and run freezes
  • implementing the training, calibration, abstention and evaluation library with its test suite
  • training on Colab GPUs
  • analysing the results and publishing the README, figures and interactive project page
project.key_learnings:
• How to run an ML experiment like a study: pre-register the hypotheses and rules, freeze decisions before seeing outcomes, and log every amendment.
  • Why leakage control (leaf-level grouping, perceptual-hash de-duplication, cross-dataset checks) has to happen before training, not after.
  • Calibration metrics in depth: ECE binning choices, Brier conventions, NLL, and why temperature scaling can’t fix a domain shift.
  • Selective prediction: risk coverage curves, AURC, and why source thresholds fail when confidence saturates near 1.0.
  • Using cluster and paired bootstrap intervals, and reporting negative and null results honestly instead of over claiming a model win.
  • Building a reproducible, hash verified pipeline on limited free GPU compute.

related.title: Residential Energy Forecasting Under Changing Conditions
related.short_description: A leakage safe, pre-registered study of how forecasting models, input choices, retraining policies and prediction intervals hold up when a house moves from winter into spring. It forecasts household electricity use 10 minutes, 1 hour and 1 day ahead, and reads a frozen 33-day test period exactly once.
